summary_note: Section 5.33. Does the probe's own prune-target selection beat the cheap load rule that section 5.32 validated on the non-probe paths? Both primaries are on the FUSED loss, signed so a win is the primary's prediction: fused(A) - fused(M) < 0 and fused(A) - fused(Q) < 0. The quietest rule isolates the TARGET - it fires only when the probe's own pick is a prune, and then takes the least-loaded expert in the probed pool - so the A-vs-Q contrast differs in the prune target alone. All four selections share the fixed arm and the probe pool.
